transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-29 09:30 UTC | Duration 54m | Recording: on
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Aisha (Nebulon Head of Search), Tom (Nebulon ML Eng), Maya (Nebulon Platform)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros from our side, I'm Lena Park, I'm the AE, and Daniel is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Daniel: hi all, yep, i'll be walking through the hosted api demo and the rerank flow, and happy to answer infra and perf Qs.
[00:14] Aisha: thanks, lena and daniel. i'm Aisha, i run search at Nebulon. we own product search, and we're looking to improve relevance and reduce latency, we currently use an open-source stack with a vector db.
[00:26] Tom: Tom here, ML infra. curious about latency at scale and how caching works, and also encryption/KMS stuff.
[00:33] Maya: and i'm Maya from platform, i'll be looking at network/VPC and deployment constraints.
[00:38] Daniel: great. quick agenda: 1) short overview of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranker endpoints, 2) console tour (tracing, token cost), 3) live demo: two-stage search (annoy/vec DB + Redwood rerank), 4) Q&A and pilot next steps.

[02:05] [Slide share] Daniel: so for hosted api we expose an embeddings endpoint and a separate rerank endpoint. typical pattern is: embed corpus -> index in your vector db -> retrieve top-K -> call rerank to rescore top results. rerank runs a cross-encoder on the snippet+query to improve fine-grained ordering.
[03:10] Aisha: is that a separate model from the embedder? what's the cost profile?
[03:18] Daniel: yes, usually different models. embedding model is smaller and cheaper per call, rerank is heavier per-doc but only called on top-K. cost depends on top-K and document length but in practice we see 80-90% of tokens on rerank when top-K is 10-20. our console shows per-route cost breakdown so you can tune top-K.

[05:00] [00:05:00] Daniel: demo time. i'll open the console. note: console shows token-level cost, latency histogram, and per-request trace with KV cache hits. here's a live example using Nebulon's sample product catalog.
[05:30] [00:05:30] (audio: typing)
[06:01] Daniel: okay i issued a query: "waterproof hiking jacket women's". retrieval returned 50 candidates from the vector DB, then we call rerank with K=20. you'll see the rerank trace, it shows cross-attention time and kv cache warmup.
[07:20] Tom: the kv cahce, is that per-session or global? we've seen issues with cache invalidation in our self-hosted stack.
[07:30] Daniel: good question — it's prefix and KV caching per model instance. for hosted we maintain per-customer namespaces for KV so cold-starts are minimized; invalidation can be manual via an API or time-based TTL. Note: sometimes transcripts show it as "KV cahce" in logs, apologies for that, auto transcript quirk.

[09:10] Aisha: what's the end-to-end latency here for rerank on K=20?
[09:16] Daniel: in this demo ~180-220ms for rerank calls with our 8-bit quant model on dedicated instances; on hosted multitenant you'd see slightly higher median but we have SLO options and can run dedicated pools. overall E2E with retrieval tends to be 250-400ms depending on vector DB latency.
[10:45] Maya: you mentioned dedicated pools — do we need to commit to Dedicated capacity or can we start hosted then move?
[10:53] Lena: you can absolutely start with hosted, then when you need predictable throughput you can shift to Dedicated. migration is a config change and model pinning in the console. many customers start hosted to validate quality then reserve capacity.

[12:30] Tom: for data residency, do you support region pinning? we have EU-only requirements for some product lines.
[12:36] Daniel: region pinning is supported. hosted has region routing and we can ensure data stays in EU regions. for stricter requirements there's Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). SOC2 and audit logs are available for enterprise tiers.

[14:05] Aisha: curious about evaluation: how do you help avoid regressions when we change prompts or upgrade models?
[14:12] Daniel: Redwood Optimize gives quality monitoring — you can attach prompt sets and we run automatic evals and surface regression alerts. Also console supports A/B rollouts for model variants.

[16:40] [00:16:40] Daniel: switching to cost tuning: we recommend 1) reduce top-K for rerank if retrieval quality is high, 2) use prefix/KV caching for sessiony traffic, 3) quantized rerank models for lower cost with small quality tradeoffs. here's a cost example: if you reduce top-K from 20 to 10, you cut rerank token cost roughly in half.
[17:25] Tom: do you have recommended thresholds for recall vs precision tradeoffs? our PM cares about conversion so precision is important.
[17:33] Daniel: a common approach is to tune for recall in retrieval (bigger K) then use rerank to sort on precision. but if cost is sensitive, smaller K with stronger retriever + stored metadata features can do well. we can help run some model comparisons during the pilot.

[20:55] Aisha: security specifics: SSO/SAML support? audit logs? encryption at rest with KMS?
[21:03] Lena: yes to all — SSO and SAML for console, RBAC to restrict routes, audit logs are available and you can integrate with SIEM, and we support KMS/HSM for key management. for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS too.

[23:40] Maya: networking: we want to avoid public egress from our prod VPC. can the hosted API be accessed from a private endpoint?
[23:48] Daniel: hosted has private link options in major cloud providers; Redwood Private gives full in-VPC control. For the hosted pilot we can set up a VPC peering / private link so traffic stays on internal network.

[26:00] Aisha: benchmarks — we'd like to see real numbers on our data. can you run a short run using our sample logs and share cost/latency?
[26:08] Daniel: yes we can do a benchmark run. ideally you'll share a 1-2k query sample and corresponding doc snippets, and we'll run retrieval+r erank and return median latency and cost per 1k queries.

[28:12] [00:28:12] (demo pause) Daniel: quick note on rate limits: hosted has per-tenant rate limits but can be raised for pilot. when you move to Dedicated you get predictable throughput. also there's automatic fallback policies to cheaper model variants if capacity constrained.

[31:01] Tom: any thoughts on vector DB choices? we're on an open-source vector db but wonder if we should move to managed.
[31:10] Daniel: Redwood is DB-agnostic — we integrate with most vector DBs. If you want simpler ops, some customers use managed vector DBs (Pinecone, Weaviate) and still call Redwood for rerank. The retrieval quality needs to be tuned, but we support end-to-end connectors.

[34:20] Aisha: what about throughput — expected QPS for a 50k daily active user app?
[34:27] Daniel: depends a lot on query distribution, but rough math: if you have 5 qps sustained with peaks higher, hosted can handle it but Dedicated gives cost predictability. we'll take your expected peak QPS and estimated docs per query as part of pilot planning.

[36:50] Maya: compliance paperwork — we will need SOC2 cert and ATO artifacts, can you send them?
[36:56] Lena: yes, we'll share our SOC2 report and security pack. we'll include network diagrams and pen test summary.

[39:30] Aisha: good. are there any pitfalls customers hit when migrating from self-hosted rerank to Redwood?
[39:37] Daniel: common issues: relying on very large top-K in retrieval (costly), not leveraging KV/prefix cache patterns, and forgetting to pin model versions during rollouts. we help with runbooks and config suggestions in Redwood Optimize.

[42:10] [00:42:10] Lena: ok let's talk pilot scope. proposed: 1-week pilot, 1k-2k queries/day simulated, use your sample logs, run hosted rerank with K=20 and a tuned retriever baseline, produce latency/cost and relevance delta. Success metrics: increase in MRR or CTR on top result by X% (customer to confirm) and median E2E latency under 350ms.
[43:05] Aisha: that sounds reasonable. I'll confirm target metric (likely CTR uplift on purchase clicks).

[45:00] Tom: who will own infra setup for the VPC peering?
[45:05] Maya: our platform team will. we'll need the peering instructions and security contacts.
[45:12] Lena: we'll cc infra docs and an onboarding guide. Daniel will handle the benchmark setup.

[47:30] Daniel: quick live note — the console allows you to replay traces and export them, and the Optimize page will suggest quant profiles and batching settings based on workload. there's a small UI hiccup in the demo environment where model names sometimes render oddly, ignore that — it's a staging artifact.

[50:11] Aisha: any upfront cost for the pilot?
[50:16] Lena: for a short validation pilot we usually provide credits and discounted pilot pricing. we'll include that in the pricing email.

[52:30] Maya: timeline check: we need SOC2 docs and pilot planning by next week to hit our July sprint.
[52:36] Lena: we'll send docs today and propose pilot kickoff 2026-07-06.
[53:00] Lena: recap: Lena sends pricing+security docs; Daniel runs benchmark with sample logs once Tom shares them; schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-07-06. thanks everyone.
[53:14] (call ends)
